L48: ### Exploratory Field Trial to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of BI 705564 in Dogs with B-cell Lymphoma
L49: 
L50: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L51: #### SUMMARY OF STUDY:
L52: 
L53: Lymphoma is the most common malignancy in dogs, with B-cell lymphomas accounting for ~70% of all canine lymphomas. There is an unmet need for effective treatments for canine B-cell lymphoma. The standard of care for dogs with B-cell lymphoma provides relatively short median overall survival times despite high remission rates. Side effects are common and may be dose-limiting.
L54: B-cell lymphoma occurs as a result of neoplastic transformation and clonal expansion of B-lymphocytes. Aberrant expression of multiple components of B-cell receptor (BCR) signaling has been demonstrated in canine B-cell lymphoma. Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) plays a crucial role in oncogenic signaling downstream of the BCR that is critical for the proliferation and survival of B-cells in many B-cell malignancies.
L55: The BTK inhibitor BI 705564 has the potential to achieve marked clinical responses in dogs with B-cell malignancies and addresses major unmet needs. These include the expected improvement of quality of life with minimal side effects, increased survival time, oral administration, and affordability. These characteristics will empower general practitioners to treat canine lymphoma and increase accessibility to care for dogs with lymphoma.
L56: This study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of BI 705564 in dogs with treatment-naïve B-cell lymphoma.
L57: #### INCLUSION CRITERIA:
L58: 
L59: Dogs >1 year of age and weighing between 10-50 kg
L60: 
L61: At least two lymph nodes measuring >2 cm in largest diameter
L62: 
L63: Dogs cannot have received systemic corticosteroid treatment for more than 2 weeks and/or within 5 days prior to screening
L64: 
L65: No prior chemotherapy (cytotoxic chemotherapy, verdinexor/Laverdia) or radiation therapy.
L66: 
L67: No current immunotherapy treatment (e.g. monoclonal antibodies: beimvetmab/Librela, lokivetmab/Cytopoint).
L68: 
L69: Stage II, III, or IV B-cell lymphoma
L70: #### FINANCIAL INCENTIVES:
L71: 
L72: Participating pet owners will receive:
L73: 
L74: Screening testing, including blood work, urinalysis, chest x-rays, abdominal ultrasound, flow cytometry, and IDEXX Cancer Dx Panel are covered. Once enrolled, the study is fully funded.
L75: #### WHAT TO EXPECT:
L76: 
L77: Participating patients will be required to complete standard pre-enrollment screening that involves a physical exam, blood work, urinalysis, lymph node testing, radiographs, and ultrasound. Dogs are seen weekly, then every 2 weeks for a study duration of 12 weeks. Owners will administer oral BI 705565 daily with a meal. We will monitor blood work and lymph node size to evaluate safety and efficacy.

L59: ### Canine B-Cell Lymphoma Study
L60: 
L61: Now Enrolling Patients​
L62: 
L63: #### Study Overview
L64: 
L65: The primary objective of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of an oral treatment for dogs newly diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma.
L66: 
L67: #### Eligibility Criteria
L68: 
L69:   * Dog is > 1 year old
L70:   * Dog is ≥ 22lbs ≤ 100 lbs
L71:   * Dog has been diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma and is treatment naive
L72: 
L73: #### Study Timeline
L74: 
L75:   * 3 months
L76:   * 10 clinic visits per patient
L77: ### Interested in this study?
L78: Reach out to a participating hospital to learn more!

L48: Research is different in that it looks at the use of diagnostic and treatment options that are not considered part of routine medical care. This may include the administration of novel experimental medications or the use of new diagnostic devices that are being evaluated as possible future routine medical care. It can also include the collection of extra patient samples (i.e., blood, urine, tissue) to be used for research studies at a later date.
L49: By enrolling your pet in a research study, you are committing to helping us improve the way that we care for our patients in the future. Many studies will allow your pet to receive treatment or have a diagnostic procedure performed that would not otherwise be available to them. There will also be many studies in which the study does not immediately benefit your pet, but the data collected will benefit other pets and humans in the future.
L50: The potential benefits to your pet will always be discussed by your doctor prior to you electing to enroll your pet in a study.
L51: ##
L52: 
L53: ### Any Cancer Type
L54: 
L55: #### 【19†Canine Oncology Study for Myc Inhibition Tolerability Trial (COSMyc- IT)】
L56: 
L57: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L58: 
L59: Myc is one of the most frequently amplified oncogenes in most human cancers and often correlates with aggressiveness of the disease. Many different types of cancer take advantage of this molecular pathway. Inhibition of this pathway may lead to a decrease in tumor size or improvement in overall condition.
L60: 
L61: 【19†STUDY DETAILS >】

L65: ### Hemoabdomen & Hemangiosarcoma
L66: #### 【20†Ethos Precision Medicine Umbrella Study for Hemangiosarcoma (ePUSH)】
L67: 
L68: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L69: 
L70: Is your dog undergoing surgery for a ruptured splenic tumor? Ethos Discovery would love to have you and your dog participate in our clinical trial! We are evaluating drugs for the treatment of HSA with the goal of curing this aggressive cancer.
L71: 
L72: 【20†STUDY DETAILS >】
L73: #### 【21†An indication-seeking pilot study of Paccal Vet in dogs with Splenic Hemangiosarcoma following splenectomy】
L74: 
L75: CLOSED
L76: 
L77: Paclitaxel is one of the most effective anticancer agents used in human cancer today, with potent activity against a wide variety of tumors. Paccal Vet may be a promising treatment option for dogs with hemangiosarcoma.
L78: 
L79: 【21†STUDY DETAILS >】

L83: ### Lymphoma
L84: #### 【22†Exploratory Field Trial to Investigate Efficacy and Safety of BI 705564 in Dogs with B-cell Lymphoma】
L85: 
L86: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L87: 
L88: The BTK inhibitor BI 705564 has the potential to achieve marked clinical responses in dogs with B-cell malignancies and addresses major unmet needs. These include the expected improvement of quality of life with minimal side effects, increased survival time, oral administration, and affordability.
L89: 
L90: 【22†STUDY DETAILS >】
L91: #### 【23†Stratification of Outcomes for Lymphoma in Dogs】
L92: 
L93: CLOSED
L94: 
L95: This study focuses on better understanding the genetics behind canine lymphoma. By studying changes in the DNA of these cancers, researchers hope to identify patterns that could lead to more personalized treatment options.
L96: 
L97: 【23†STUDY DETAILS >】
L98: 
L99: ##
L100: 
L101: ### Osteosarcoma (Bone Cancer)
L102: #### 【24†Biobanking Osteosarcoma as a Nexus for Evaluation and Staging (BONES)】
L103: 
L104: CURRENTLY ENROLLING
L105: 
L106: The BONES study seeks to create a “biobank” by collecting tissue and blood samples from dogs with osteosarcoma over time. These valuable samples will be shared with leading bone cancer researchers to help them better understand why this cancer spreads and becomes resistant to treatment.
L107: 
L108: 【24†STUDY DETAILS >】
L109: #### 【25†Autologous canine cancer vaccine with checkpoint inhibitor for treatment of Osteosarcoma】
L110: 
L111: CLOSED
L112: 
L113: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of an autologous killed tumor cell vaccine. this trial aims to advance safer, immune-based treatment options for canine cancer that may offer comparable or superior outcomes to chemotherapy.
L114: 
L115: 【25†STUDY DETAILS >】

L117: ## FAQs
L118: ### How is research different from regular medical care?
L119: 
L120: Research is different in that it looks at the use of diagnostic and treatment options that are not considered part of routine medical care. This may include the administration of novel experimental medications or the use of new diagnostic devices that are being evaluated as possible future routine medical care. It can also include the collecting of extra patient samples (i.e., blood, urine, tissue) to be used for research studies at a later date.
L121: ### As a pet owner, what is expected of me if I enroll my pet in a clinical study?
L122: 
L123: Each study is set up according to its needs. We encourage you to read the guidelines associated with the study you are interested in.
L124: 
L125: In General:
L126: 
L127: Compensation for enrolling your pet in a study will differ for each study. Usually, it consists of the diagnostics and treatments that are part of the study being provided to you at no cost. Additionally, there could be other discounts applied to the care of your pet.
L128: In some cases, you may be asked to give medications to your pet, alter their diet, or exercise plans. This will vary for each study. Some studies will require the administration of certain medications or other treatments. Others might require questionnaires to be filled out before or after the study.
L129: The duration of each research study will vary depending on the study design. Simple studies generally require a one-time interaction with a patient with no need for follow up. More comprehensive studies will follow patients over a longer period of time, such as several months or up to one year.
L130: The data collected from your pet will be used to improve the care that we provide to future patients. It will be used to show that a new treatment works with good efficacy or that a novel diagnostic test is accurate. Data collected from patients will be used in scientific publications and presentations in order to inform other veterinarians around the world about the research that we’ve done so they can adopt similar treatments and diagnostics in their practices.
L131: All patient data is anonymized and is not shared with any third parties.
L132: ### What if I decide to participate in a research study but change my mind at a later date?
L133: 
L134: All studies provide the option to unenroll your pet at any time. There are no negative consequences should you elect to have them removed from a study.
